Scope extended back to Peter I's governorates (29 Dec 1708); before the namestnichestva every atom is named unresolved.

sources.says: Kazan changes 1781–1895; the only one across the outer line is 17 Feb 1895 (ПСЗ-3 № 11373): three Yaransk villages (Viatka) joined Tsarevokokshaisk uyezd.

sources.title: Вятская губерния — Википедия (oldid 154631147)

sources.title: Симбирская губерния — Википедия (oldid 154934454)

sources.title: Пермская губерния — Википедия (oldid 152904819)

sources.title: Тобольское наместничество — Википедия (oldid 154778678)
sources.says: Founded by decree of 19 Jan 1782 (№ 15327) from the territory of the abolished Tobolsk province, with Tobolsk and Tomsk oblasts; opened 30 Aug 1782.

spans.dateNote: ПСЗ-1 № 15307, 1781-12-23 O.S. (Chelyabinsk uyezd to Ufa namestnichestvo) = 1782-01-03. Perm namestnichestvo until 12 Dec 1796 O.S., then Perm governorate; the 1796 abolition of Alapaevsk, Dalmatov, Obvinsk uyezds was internal. Den prints the founding decree as 27.01.1787 — a misprint for 1781 (ПСЗ-1 № 15113). The Tobolsk namestnichestvo founded east of it on 19 Jan 1782 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 15327) was the remnant of the Siberian governorate's Tobolsk province after Perm had been cut out, so it did not move the Perm line (the same treatment as the 1781 Moscow namestnichestvo in RUE-central).
